scenes.text: Your agents spend most of their day waiting. Why is every one of them still holding memory?
scenes.say: Your agents spend most of the day waiting. So why is every one of them still holding memory?

scenes.headline: How Agent Substrate makes an idle agent cheap
scenes.sub: Snapshots, warm workers, and where the density comes from
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Brielle! Agent Substrate is a Kubernetes runtime that turns a waiting agent into a snapshot. Let's see how, and what its density claim measures.

scenes.title: An agent mostly waits
scenes.sub: And Kubernetes offers two bad options
scenes.say: Chapter one. An agent mostly waits.

scenes.title: One turn of a coding agent
scenes.say: Follow one turn of a coding agent.

items.say: It sends the conversation to a model and waits for tokens.
It runs a tool, a search or a test. Only this part works the sandbox.
Then it waits for a person: minutes, hours, or a day.

scenes.title: Two bad options, one way out

left.title: Pods on Kubernetes
items: One pod per session holds memory while idle
Deleting pods costs seconds and the state
left.say: Kubernetes gives you two bad options. Keep a pod per session and pay for idle memory. Or delete pods between turns, and pay a cold start and the lost state.

right.title: Actors on warm workers
right.say: Substrate takes a third way. A waiting agent becomes a snapshot, and comes back on whichever warm worker is free.

scenes.title: Actors on warm workers
scenes.sub: Swap the agent out, keep its memory
scenes.say: Chapter two. Actors on warm workers.

scenes.text: Freeze an idle agent, memory and files, into a snapshot. Restore it onto any free warm worker when the next request arrives.
scenes.say: Here's the idea. Freeze an idle agent, memory and files, into a snapshot. When the next request arrives, restore it onto any free warm worker.

status: Every actor is a snapshot. The workers wait, already warm.
Requests arrive: three actors are restored into free slots.
One goes idle. SuspendActor checkpoints it and frees its slot.
A different actor wakes into that slot. Any free worker will do.

steps.say: Picture a fleet of actors, each a stateful agent. While they wait, each is just a snapshot in storage, and the worker pods sit warm and empty.
Requests arrive. Three actors are restored, memory and all, into free slots.

steps.term: SuspendActor: checkpoint and free the slot
steps.say: One finishes its turn. A suspend call checkpoints it back to storage, freeing its slot.
A request comes for a different actor. It wakes into the freed slot. Any free worker will do.
A request names its actor in a header and reaches the router: Envoy, with a small processor in front.

steps.term: Lease: one resume per actor at a time
steps.say: If the actor is suspended, the router asks the control plane to resume it. Under a lease, the scheduler samples two workers with room and takes the less loaded.
On that node, a supervisor restores the snapshot into a sandbox, from a local copy if it has one, else from the bucket.
Then the router tunnels the request in, over mutual TLS.

scenes.credit: Agent Substrate docs, actor call diagram
scenes.title: The project's own map

steps.say: The project draws the same path, numbered: route, resume, restore from the snapshot bucket, deliver.
And on the way out, every tool call goes through the egress gateway, which holds the credentials.

steps.term: Golden snapshot: one warm boot per template
steps.say: Each template is booted once and checkpointed. New actors start from that golden snapshot, so none pays a cold boot.
A request resumes it. A cold start has become a memory restore.
While it runs, it holds a slot at its full memory limit.
When your harness calls suspend, the checkpoint lands on the node's disk and the call returns.
The upload follows five minutes later, and the local copy stays for thirty, so a quick wake skips the download.

scenes.title: Where 10x comes from
scenes.sub: The multiple is a property of the workload
scenes.say: Chapter three. Where ten x comes from.

scenes.title: Density, from first principles
scenes.text: density = N x M / (S x (M + o))
scenes.say: Take a fleet of N agents, each with a memory limit M.

parts.note: one sandbox per agent holds every limit
parts.say: One sandbox per agent holds N times M, all the time.

parts.note: only running actors hold a slot
parts.say: Multiplexed, only the S running actors hold a slot, each at its limit plus a small runtime overhead.

parts.note: tends to one over the running share
parts.say: If agents run a tenth of the time and never collide, S is a tenth of N, and the ratio is ten. The multiple is the duty cycle.

steps.say: Perfect staggering gives ten x at any size. But you size a pool for busy moments, not averages.
Sized for the ninety-ninth percentile, two hundred and fifty agents get six point eight x.
Only at a million agents does it reach nine point nine. That is why millions and ten x travel together.

scenes.title: What zero trust means here
scenes.sub: Identity, a gateway, and keys kept outside
scenes.say: Chapter four. What zero trust means here.

scenes.title: Read from the code
scenes.say: Zero trust has a definite shape in this code.

items.say: Every running actor gets its own short-lived certificate.
All outbound traffic goes through one gateway. No rule, or a failed lookup, means no traffic.
The agent sends a placeholder header, and the gateway swaps in the real key outside the sandbox.

scenes.title: Where it falls short today
scenes.say: The code also shows what is not there yet.

items.say: Nothing in this commit decides an agent is idle. Your harness calls suspend.
The benchmark harness is in the repository. The run behind the ten x is not.

items.text: The demo's key is in the sandbox
items.say: And the Claude Code demo puts its API key in plain environment variables.

scenes.text: Idle agents become snapshots, so you pay for the ones running. The density is your duty cycle, not the runtime.
scenes.mark: The density is your duty cycle
scenes.say: Idle agents become snapshots, so you pay only for the ones running. The density is your duty cycle. Measure it first.

recap: Density tends to one over the running share
Keys stay at the gateway, not the demo
scenes.say: To recap. Idle actors live as snapshots and wake on warm workers. Density tends to one over their running share. Keep keys at the gateway.
